programs.name: Nebraska veterans: county veterans service officers for claims help
programs.organization: County veterans service officers; Nebraska Department of Veterans’ Affairs
programs.description: Free help with VA claims, pension and survivor benefits, Nebraska Veterans Aid applications and other benefits from county veterans service officers. Every county has one; some officers serve two to four neighboring counties and keep part-week hours. The Nebraska Department of Veterans’ Affairs’ State Service Office in Lincoln also files claims.
programs.next_step: Choose your county for its service officer, address and hours, and call before you go. The NDVA State Service Office is at 402-420-4021.
constraints: Many rural offices are open one to three days a week; check the hours on the county card.

programs.name: Nebraska Aging and Disability Resource Center
programs.organization: Nebraska DHHS State Unit on Aging and the Area Agencies on Aging
programs.description: Nebraska’s Aging and Disability Resource Centers give information, referrals and help with community services and long-term care options to people 60 and older, people with disabilities of any age, and their families and caregivers. The Area Agencies on Aging run the local centers. Military service is not required.
programs.next_step: Call 844-843-6364, or choose a county above for its Area Agency on Aging.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

programs.name: Medicare counseling (Nebraska SHIP) for Nebraska
programs.organization: Nebraska Department of Insurance, State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP) and Senior Medicare Patrol (SMP)
programs.description: Free Medicare counseling from Nebraska SHIP, a division of the Nebraska Department of Insurance that does not sell insurance or endorse any company: plan choices, enrollment, costs and help paying for Medicare. Its Senior Medicare Patrol helps people report Medicare fraud and errors.
programs.next_step: Call 800-234-7119 to reach a counselor or arrange a meeting. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: Have your Medicare card and drug list ready.

programs.name: Nebraska Long-Term Care Ombudsman and abuse reporting
programs.organization: Nebraska Office of the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman
programs.description: Independent advocacy for residents of nursing homes and assisted living, through regional ombudsmen and the state office in Lincoln.
programs.next_step: Call the state ombudsman office at 402-802-5541. To report abuse or neglect of a vulnerable adult, call 800-652-1999. In an emergency, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

programs.name: Free legal help for Nebraska veterans and older adults
programs.description: Legal Aid of Nebraska gives free civil legal help to people with low incomes across the state through its AccessLine. Its Elder AccessLine gives Nebraskans 60 and older free legal advice and help, working with the Area Agencies on Aging.
programs.next_step: Call the Legal Aid of Nebraska AccessLine at 877-250-2016. If you are 60 or older, call the Elder AccessLine at 800-527-7249 (402-827-5656 in Omaha).
constraints: The general AccessLine screens by income and case type.

programs.name: VA health care systems serving Nebraska
programs.description: Most Nebraska veterans are served by the VA Nebraska-Western Iowa Health Care System (Omaha VA Medical Center, 4101 Woolworth Avenue; 402-346-8800), with clinics including Lincoln and Grand Island. In the Panhandle, the Scottsbluff clinic is run by the VA Black Hills Health Care System in Hot Springs, South Dakota, and the Sidney clinic by the Cheyenne VA Medical Center.
programs.next_step: Use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code to find the closest clinic. Not enrolled yet? Ask your county veterans service officer for help applying.
constraints: Which system serves you depends on where you live; VA’s locator shows the right clinic.

coverage_scope: Referral edition. All 93 counties have a county veterans service officer (some officers serve two to four counties), an Area Agency on Aging (eight agencies), the state long-term care ombudsman and a Center for Independent Living.
coverage_note: County veterans service office phones, locations and hours come from the Nebraska Department of Veterans’ Affairs directory updated October 1, 2024. Area Agencies on Aging come from the Nebraska Judicial Branch’s Office of Public Guardian list, with phones from the DHHS State Unit on Aging. The long-term care ombudsman line comes from the state ombudsman’s contact map. Independent living centers come from the ILRU national directory. Reviewed November 16, 2026. Contacts are not telephone-confirmed.
share_description: county veterans service offices, Area Agencies on Aging and long-term care ombudsman help across Nebraska
